clue.text: Streaks round across front of nudist beach

indicators.note: one piece lies across the other, spanning it on both sides
turned round, so the word for streaks is read backwards

parts.note: to streak is to dash or dart along at speed

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A naked runner dashes around the edge of a naturist beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns DARTS into STRAD; 'across' puts that around N, the first letter of nudist given by 'front of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a literary word for a shore or seashore, the stretch of land beside the water.

clue.text: Uber turning up at 11

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the short word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An Uber driver arriving at eleven o'clock, perhaps for a late pickup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' flips AT to TA; it reads as 'arriving' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Uber is a ride-hailing service, so an Uber is effectively a hired cab.

clue.text: American star Hank modelled Russian fur

indicators.note: modelled means shaped or moulded, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A US celebrity called Hank showed off a Russian fur on the catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelled' rearranges A, STAR and HANK together.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is the curly fleece of young karakul lambs, named after a city on the Volga in Russia.

clue.text: Tired, raising weapon last thing on Friday

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising lifts the word so it is read bottom to top

parts.note: a sword is a bladed weapon

indicators.note: the last thing on a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone worn out at the end of the working week, lifting a weapon late on Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns SWORD into DROWS; 'last thing on' takes Y from Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsy describes being sleepy and heavy-eyed, as a weary person is.

clue.text: Old Tyler wearing the tartan; it's a power thing

indicators.note: the kilt is worn around the other letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: the kilt is the tartan garment of Highland dress
Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A historical rebel in Highland dress is described as some sort of power figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' signals the garment going around the rest. Wat Tyler was the leader of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt; 'power thing' hides a unit of measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilowatt is a unit of power equal to a thousand watts, so it is a thing that measures power.

clue.text: Record success on the stock market (FTSE) with Moly trading

parts.note: to make a killing is to win a big profit, especially on shares

indicators.note: trading means dealing or exchanging, so these letters swap places

explanation.surface: A record day on the London index, with a commodity called Moly changing hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trading' rearranges FTSE and MOLY. The FTSE is the main London stock index; 'Record' looks like a market high but means a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hit song, recorded by Roberta Flack in 1973 and later by the Fugees, so it names a record.

clue.text: Album featuring a bit too much drama?

definitions.meaning: a record of the old twelve-inch format, played at thirty-three rpm
a theatre piece that drags on, an overlong stage drama

explanation.surface: A record that includes a touch too much theatrical fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: An LP is a full-length album record, and read literally the phrase describes a stage show that runs on.

clue.text: Mayfair party with Veuve Cliquot?

parts.note: Mayfair has the London postcode W1, written here as WI
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A smart London party with champagne flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Veuve is French for a woman whose husband has died: the champagne house is named after the widow Clicquot.
explanation.definitionFit: Veuve Clicquot was the name of a woman who ran the house after her husband died, so she is an example.

clue.text: 24 bandwagon back in the day, an occasional feature on the front of The Sun?

definitions.meaning: the van carrying the rock band of 24, fronted by Freddie Mercury, in their early touring days

definitions.text: an occasional feature on the front of The Sun?
definitions.meaning: the rare passage of the innermost planet across the solar disc

explanation.surface: A tabloid's front page recalls the band's old touring van.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 points to the band whose singer was Freddie Mercury; a Ford Transit is the classic British van.
explanation.definitionFit: A planetary transit is a crossing of the solar disc, seen roughly thirteen times a century for the innermost planet.

clue.text: Latest opinion is to place the Head on leave

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: an exit is a departure or leaving
poll is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A school plans to put the headteacher on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Head' looks like a headteacher; it is POLL, an old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit poll is a survey of voters leaving polling stations, the most recent snapshot of opinion.

clue.text: Agreed Kelly has unusual piercing

indicators.note: the odd word pierces the name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Ned Kelly was a famous Australian bushranger
odd means unusual

explanation.surface: Someone named Kelly has an unusual body piercing, and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piercing' reads as body jewellery but signals one piece inside another; Kelly is the Australian outlaw Ned Kelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head signals assent, so to have nodded is to have agreed.

clue.text: Fixing wiretaps on US secret agent

indicators.note: fixing means repairing or rigging, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Planting bugs on American phone lines for a covert operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixing' rearranges WIRETAPS ON US.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin Powers is the spoof spy played by Mike Myers in the film comedies.

clue.text: Protective covering — could be for 5D, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase means the words are said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: the 5-down song was sung by Roberta Flack, so its record sleeve would be her jacket

explanation.surface: A protective coat that might suit the song at 5 down.
explanation.walkthrough: A record sleeve is called a jacket in the US; Roberta Flack sang the 5-down hit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bulletproof or shrapnel-proof vest worn by soldiers and police for protection.

clue.text: Insipid interior of Puebla Hotel

indicators.note: the interior of the phrase holds the letters needed, running inside it

explanation.surface: A dull inside to a hotel in the Mexican city of Puebla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior of' takes letters running across Puebla Hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah describes something bland and uninteresting, lacking flavour or spirit.

clue.text: Emergency procedure with Oscar Alpha coming in to land!

indicators.note: the two letters come inside the other word

parts.note: to ground is to bring down to land
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Alpha is A in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A pilot calls for an emergency manoeuvre as aircraft come in to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' places O and A inside GROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Aborting a landing and circling for another approach is a standard safety manoeuvre in aviation.

clue.text: See 8
United, Delta flying from Auld Reekie turning over water

indicators.note: the two letters fly away out of the phrase
turning over means upending, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Airline flights leaving Edinburgh for somewhere across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Auld Reekie is a nickname for Edinburgh. 'flying from' removes U and D; 'turning over' rearranges ALREEKIE.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America, a large body of freshwater.

clue.text: Acne irks — applied moisturiser?

definitions.note: a moisturiser is one example of the category, hence the question mark

indicators.note: applied means put to work or worked on, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spots are a nuisance, so on goes the moisturiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied' rearranges ACNE IRKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Moisturising cream is a typical product for looking after the complexion, an example of the category.

clue.text: Post Neeson rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Liam Neeson is the Northern Irish actor

explanation.surface: A letter turning down the actor Liam Neeson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns LIAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Post and mail are synonyms for letters and parcels sent through the postal system.

clue.text: Commercial diamonds smuggled by State Head of Transport

indicators.note: the stones are smuggled inside the other word

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A state transport chief is caught smuggling diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smuggled by' puts D inside AVER; 'Head of' takes T from Transport. 'State' and 'Head' look like an official's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial on television or radio is an advertisement.

clue.text: Came to a point about my 24 answerphone?

indicators.note: the first word goes about, around, the second

parts.note: something tapered narrows to a point
cor is an exclamation like my!
the answer at 24 is the monarch, ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: Getting to the point about the monarch's phone messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals one piece enclosing another. The 24-across monarch is Elizabeth, whose royal cipher is Elizabeth Regina; 'my' is the exclamation cor!
explanation.definitionFit: Old answering machines recorded callers' messages on cassette, so one is an example.

clue.text: More Artex mixture!

indicators.note: a mixture is a blend, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A call for more textured coating for the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: Artex is a British textured wall and ceiling finish. 'mixture' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, as when asking for some on top.

clue.text: Turn over telly screening English opener Boycott

indicators.note: the turned letters screen, or enclose, the next one
turn means the letters are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
telly is British slang for television, TV

indicators.note: an opener is the first letter of a word

explanation.surface: Switching the TV over to watch the England batsman Geoffrey Boycott.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' makes VTO from O and TV; 'screening' holds E inside. Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England opening batsman, so 'Boycott' looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto is to forbid or reject, much as a boycott refuses something.

clue.text: Get runs following Fish Curry?

definitions.note: John Curry was a British Olympic figure-skating champion

indicators.note: the letter for runs follows the fish

parts.note: skate is a flat fish
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An upset stomach after a fish curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry' reads as the dish; it is John Curry, the 1976 Olympic figure-skating champion.
explanation.definitionFit: He is an example of someone who performs on ice, hence the question mark.

clue.text: It follows; after disco, nurse makes toast

parts.note: in the word discotheque, these letters follow the opening disco
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A late-night celebration: the nurse raises a glass after the disco.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks what comes after DISCO in a longer word: discotheque.
explanation.definitionFit: The loyal toast to the monarch is drunk at formal British dinners.

clue.text: Approach vast rat Egyptian's trapped

indicators.note: the words have the letters trapped inside them

explanation.surface: A plan for catching an enormous rodent in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped' takes letters running across vast rat Egyptian's.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a plan or method, a way of tackling something.

clue.text: Beckett character's retiring, having a yen to visit Chihuahua

indicators.note: the letter goes in to visit, sitting inside the name
retiring means drawing back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Godot is the never-arriving figure in Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Godot, at last, wanders off to Mexico on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns GODOT into TODOG; 'to visit' puts Y inside. 'Chihuahua' looks like the Mexican state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chihuahua is a tiny breed kept as a pet, an example of a small companion breed.
